newsitem.title: PERU: Lima shrs drop in low volume, investors sidelined.
newsitem.headline: Lima shrs drop in low volume, investors sidelined.

text.p: Shares on the Lima stock exchange continued Monday last week's trend of falling prices in meager volume, due to an absence of market-moving news to attract investors off the sidelines, brokers said.
Tuesday was likely to see the same trend, they added.
On Monday, the General Index fell 0.18 percent to 1,543.37 points, while the blue-chip Selective Index dropped 0.66 percent to 2,082.10 points, according to preliminary stock figures.
In a total of 1,297 trades, 32 stocks fell, 19 rose and 32 were stable in low volume of 10.0 million ($3.9 million).
"The trade was insipid," said Enrique Hernandez of local brokerage Macrovalores. "Both foreign and local investors were sidelined waiting for third quarter results."
Companies' will begin to publish their third quarter financial results later this week.
Benchmark Telefonica del Peru accounted for 27 percent of the market's volume on Monday as it dropped 0.69 percent to 5.74 soles.
Among other leaders, Backus Johnston -- the country's largest brewery -- rose 0.38 percent to 2.64 with six percent of total volume.
Electricity distributor Luz del Sur, which will see up to 30 percent of its state-held shares sold next month, climbed 1.47 percent to 3.46 soles.
